title: Khmer Consonants and Vowels
intro: Modern Khmer uses a wrting system consisting of 44 independent consonant symbols (33 regular symbols and 11 others modified by the diacritics (៉) and ( ៊ ) ). The principle of the writing system is that each independent symbol represents, not an isolated consonant or vowel (as in a strictly alphabetic system), but a syllable. Thuseach consonant symbol represents a spoken consonant © followed by a spoken vowel (V). There are 12 independent vowel symbols and 16 conjunct (or dependent) vowel symbols which serve in various combinations with the consonant symbols. The vowel symbols are pronounced in two different ways, according to the set to which they belong. (Ref: Communicating in Khmer Software, by Chhany Sak Humphry)

title: Learn to spelling Khmer Script
intro:
Words with no written vowel --
Many Khmer words consist of simply two consonants, with no vowel symbol appearing, eg. ដង, មក. These words are usually pronounced with an inherent –or sound. Some common words with an initial second series consonant are, however, pronounced with an inherent –oa sound.

title: More on spelling Khmer Script
intro:
Consonant clusters and subscript
When two consonant sounds occur together at the beginning of a word  e.g: t wer, s ray, kroo, etc.  the second consonant symbol is written underneath the initial consonant. Each consonant symbol in Cambodian has in addition to its normal form a subscript form. Thus, for every consonant symbol, it is also necessary to learn a subscript form. In some cases the subscript consonant are very similar to their  parent  consonants; in other instances there is virtually no resemblance whatsoever.

Consonant clusters and vowels
If the initial consonant and subscript consonant both belong to the same series then the vowel will take that series. But if an initial consonant belonging to the first series is followed by one of the subscript consonants above, then the vowel takes the first series pronunciation.

នៅ​ក្រុង​ភ្នំ​ពេញ ផ្សារ​ដែល​មាន​ឈ្មោះ​ល្បី​ជាង​គេ គឺ​ផ្សារ​ថ្មី ​ឬ​ផ្សារ​ធំ។ ក្រៅ​ពី​នេះ​មាន​ផ្សារ​កណ្តាល ផ្សារ​ចាស់ ផ្សារអូ​ឡាំ​ពិក និង​ផ្សារអូ​ឬស្សី​ជា​ដើម។

lessons.article: If you are a foreigner in Cambodia, your most frequent conversations with Cambodians are likely to involve telling them your name, nationality and perhaps something about your work. These are the kind of statements you will probably need to be able to make about yourself.

lessons.title: នៅក្នុងភោជនីយដ្ឋាន (In the restaurant)
lessons.article: Food is cheap in Cambodia and the larger restaurants offer a variety of local, Chinese and western dishes. Usually the menu will list foods in French, English and Cambodian. In Phnom Penh’s ‘dancing restaurants’ there will be a live band and girls can be hired as dancing partners. Customers are usually there for the dancing rather than the food. Cambodian food itself is rather less spicy than Thai food. Typically a meal will consist of rice with a number of side dishes consisting of soups, salads and stir-fried dishes. In the conversation, one of the popular Cambodian dishes Sopheap orders is som-lor m’joo which is a sour soup made from mixture of tomatoes, cucumbers and pineapples cooked with basil and tamarind juice.

ចា៎ សូមចាំមួយភ្លែត

lessons.title: នៅឯផ្សារ (At the market)
lessons.article: Generally speaking, markets are excellent places to practice your Cambodian, and often, for the cost of a very small purchase, you can get a valuable language lesson from vendors. This lesson gives you practice in two basic transactions – bargaining and asking names of things. See how much of the dialogue you can read in Cambodian script now! (A=Jill; B=Vendor)
vocabulary: ឆ្ងាញ់មិនឆ្ងាញ់

items.text: សូមសួរ នេះហៅថាអ្វី?
items.speaker: A

items.text: គេហៅថា ផ្លែក្រូច។
items.speaker: B

items.text: មួយគីឡូប៉ុន្មានរៀល?
items.speaker: A

items.text: មួយគីឡូបីពាន់រៀលប៉ុណ្ណោះ។
items.speaker: B

items.text: អូ៎ ថ្លៃណាស់។ ចុះថ្លៃបន្តិចបានទេ?
items.speaker: A

items.text: ទេ មិនថ្លៃទេ។ ក្រូចនេះឆ្ងាញ់ណាស់។ លមើល ឆ្ងាញ់មិនឆ្ងាញ់។
items.speaker: B

items.text: ឆ្ងាញ់គ្រាន់បើ។ ពីរពាន់រៀលបានទេ?
items.speaker: A

items.text: មិនបានទេ។ ចង់បានប៉ុន្មានគីឡូ?
items.speaker: B

items.text: ខ្ញុំចង់បានតែមួយគីឡូទេ។
items.speaker: A

items.text: ទិញផ្លែក្រូចនៅផ្សារ

choices.text: អូ៎ ថ្លៃណាស់។
ចុះថ្លៃបន្តិច
ក្រូចនេះឆ្ងាញ់ណាស់។
ទេ មិនថ្លៃទេ។
លមើល ឆ្ងាញ់មិនឆ្ងាញ់។
ពីរពាន់រៀល
ឆ្ងាញ់គ្រាន់បើ។
ចង់បានប៉ុន្មាន
តែមួយគីឡូទេ។

lessons.title: និយាយភាសាខ្មែរ (Speaking Cambodian)
lessons.article: Cambodians are generally surprised and pleased that westerners make the effort to learn their language. Even the clumsiest attempts to say something in Cambodian are likely to be greeted with enthusiastic praise. But don’t let fulsome praise go to your head!
vocabulary: បន្តិចបន្តួច
មិន…ប៉ុន្មានទេ
អក្សរខ្មែរ
ស្តាប់មិនបានទេ

items.text: លោកចេះនិយាយភាសាខ្មែរឬទេ?
items.speaker: A

items.text: ខ្ញុំនិយាយបានបន្តិចបន្តួច។
items.speaker: B

items.text: ទេ, លោកនិយាយបានល្អណាស់។ នៅស្រុកខ្មែរយូរទេ?
items.speaker: A

items.text: មិនយូរប៉ុន្មានទេ។
items.speaker: B

items.text: លោកសរសេរអក្សរខ្មែរបានទេ?
items.speaker: A

items.text: ខ្ញុំស្តាប់មិនបានទេ។ សូមថាម្តងទៀតបានទេ?
items.speaker: B

items.text: ចា៎។ លោកសរសេរអក្សរខ្មែរបានទេ?
items.speaker: A

items.text: “អក្សរ”? ខ្ញុំមិនយល់ទេ។ ភាសាអង់គ្លេសថាអ្វី?
items.speaker: B

items.text: ភាសាអង់គ្លេសថា ‘Letter’
items.speaker: A

items.text: បាទ, អរគុណ។ យល់ហើយ។ ខ្ញុំសរសេរខ្មែរមិនបានទេ ប៉ុន្តែចង់រៀន។
items.speaker: B

ខ្ញុំអត់យល់ទេ។
ភាសាអង់គ្លេសថាអ្វី?
